# `undefined-value-escape`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: correctness · Profile: none · Default: warning · Fixes: none · Options: none

Reports a value initialized with `undefined` that is read or escapes before
whole-value initialization.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

Reading undefined bytes is illegal behavior and partial initialization can
expose invalid fields.

## When it fires

It applies to a local `var` initialized with `undefined` when the analyzer sees
the binding escape or be consumed before a proven whole-value write. A
fixed-length array is reported when an element is read before any element or
slice of it is written. A struct declared in the same file is tracked field by
field: reading a field before it is written, or using the whole value while a
field is still unwritten, is reported. Taking an address, calling a method and
passing a slice count as initialization. A use inside a loop that writes the
binding later in its body is not reported, since an earlier iteration may have
initialized it, and neither are container-level variables, which any function
may set first.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
fn f() u32 {
    var x: u32 = undefined;
    return x;
}
```
